newsitem.title: UK: Brent up on paper market, prompt spreads, cfds firm.
newsitem.headline: Brent up on paper market, prompt spreads, cfds firm.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude firmed sharply on a quiet paper market on Friday with intermonth spreads and CFDs firming as the market shrugged off underlying negative fundamental picture, traders said.
On the physical market there was unconfirmed talk of an end May Brent trading at July Brent -29 cents, or June -27 cents, a little weaker from its earlier levels.

But traders said there were at least three other third decade May Brents on offer, some at June Brent -24 cents, the last level the benchmark crude traded at this week, suggesting the grade was steady.
"There's been some Brent on offer, some (sellers) were asking for last done but I have not heard of any trades taking place. It was very quiet," one trader said.
On cash, July Brent soared to a high of $20.04 in late trade for the first time in nearly two months, and by 1734 GMT was at $19.94 a barrel, or 45 cents up on Thursday's close.
Brent intermonth spreads firmed a little with Jun/Jul at 0/+2 cents in late talk after trading earlier at evens. Jul/Aug and Aug/Sep also followed suit from -3/0 earlier.
Prompt Brent CFDs also gained further in late talk, with next week's talked four cents firmer at July Brent -20/-18.
It traded earlier at July Brent -23 cents, four cents stronger than Thursday's levels.
May 27-30 also gained, talked two cent higher at July Brent -20/-18 cents after an earlier trade at July Brent -21 cents.
Traders said the North Sea grades would get a short-term boost from June loading programmes -- mostly a little less than May's due to maintenance work.
The grades also drew support from an attractive arbitrage with the U.S.
But the market remained fundamentally week with good supplies of end May barrels around.
Traders said there were two end May Osebergs and three Ekofisks unsold. A Norwegian major said it sold on Friday one Oseberg and one Ekofisk, both end May cargoes, but the deals were confidential.
A June 8-10 Oseberg traded at a 15 cents premium to Dated Brent late on Thursday, 25 cents higher than what a third decade May cargo fetched the same day.

Traders had attributed the lower numbers fetched by the prompt Norwegian sweet crude on Thursday to higher freight cost due to the low number of vessels around, which forced the seller to cut the price.
The two Brent cargoes turning wet on Friday, the first of the June loading programme, were both five o'clocked, traders said.
Suko was clocked with one of the June 1-3 loaders and there was a dispute between Koch and Nova over the second, they added.

No deals were reported in the Mediterranean but traders said Russian Urals seemed a little stronger with third decade May cargoes offered at a $1.05 discount to Dated Brent and bid in the Dated Brent -$1.15/-$1.20 area.
Traders said that an early June Urals held by a refiner was swapped on Thursday for a May 20-24 loader of the sour crude with an independent trader.
Negotiations between Syria's state oil company Sytrol and term lifter over June prices continued but both sides were far apart.

The Syrians, prompted by Saudi Arabia's recent increase of the price of Arab Light, lifted their asking price to Dated Brent -60 cents for Syrian Light, 22 cents over May, but buyers considered bidding less than the April price of Dated Brent -95 cents.
The West African market was quiet and largely steady. There was unconfirmed talk of a mid June Brass River traded at Dated Brent +57 cents in the last two days.
--Haitham Haddadin, London newsroom +44 171 542 8145
